feedback.problem:
Consider the following trigonometric equation: 

$$
\operatorname{sin}⁡(x+\frac{\pi }{4})=-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}
$$

  

The general solution of this equation can be expressed as

$$
x=\pi +2\pi n,\,x=b\pi +2\pi n,
$$

where $n$ is any integer. Find a possible value of $b$ in the range $[0,2).$

$b=$
{{field-1}}
feedback.worked_solution:
The general solution to our equation is

$$
\begin{aligned}x+\frac{\pi }{4} & =\frac{5\pi }{4}+2\pi n, & \, & \, & x+\frac{\pi }{4} & =\frac{7\pi }{4}+2\pi n.\end{aligned}
$$

Solving the two equations above for $x,$ we get:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =\frac{5\pi }{4}-\frac{\pi }{4}+2\pi n & \, & \, & x & =\frac{7\pi }{4}-\frac{\pi }{4}+2\pi n \\ x & =\frac{4\pi }{4}+2\pi n & \, & \, & x & =\frac{6\pi }{4}+2\pi n \\ x & =\pi +2\pi n & \, & \, & x & =\frac{3\pi }{2}+2\pi n\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have that $b=\frac{3}{2}.$
